title: SSRF through a string-prefix URL allow-list
root_cause: The server fetches a URL chosen by the user and tries to restrict it with a text check, but URL syntax has several ways to put one host in the text and a different host in the request ('example.com.evil.test', userinfo '@', redirects, IP encodings). The program and the HTTP client disagree about what the URL means, so the attacker can aim the server's own network position at internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
defenses: Parse the URL with the same library that will make the request, then compare the parsed host exactly against an allow-list.
Resolve DNS yourself, reject private, loopback and link-local addresses, and connect to the resolved IP (defeats DNS rebinding).
Disable redirects or re-validate every hop.
Block egress from the service to internal ranges and to the cloud metadata address at the network layer.
Require metadata-service session tokens (IMDSv2-style) so a plain GET cannot read credentials.
